summary.oneLiner: FY26 was a regulatory-disruption reset year (revenue flat, EBITDA breakeven); FY27 thesis is a 30% growth / net-net PAT-breakeven story powered by a second growth engine (Shotgun RTD doubling) plus continued luxury/super-premium premiumization, with capex cycle largely behind it.

thesis (one line): FY26 was a regulatory-disruption reset year (revenue flat, EBITDA breakeven); FY27 thesis is a 30% growth / net-net PAT-breakeven story powered by a second growth engine (Shotgun RTD doubling) plus continued luxury/super-premium premiumization, with capex cycle largely behind it.
scorecard: One-offs: None explicitly flagged. EBITDA still includes elevated brand-build spend (Shotgun marketing >10% of its top line in launch year vs 7% normal). No exceptional items disclosed.
guidance (critical): FY27 revenue growth: ~30% YoY → implies ~INR240 cr revenue.
PAT: net-net breakeven (not just cash breakeven) targeted in FY27 at ~INR240 cr revenue.
Growth visible "even from Q1" of FY27; premiumization momentum continuing into Q1.
RTD (Shotgun): double sales in FY27 → cross 200,000 cases (from ~100,000).
Exports: target 5% of total revenue from FY27 onwards (export revenue doubled in FY26).
Gross margin: 76%–80% range going forward (RTD GM ~70% dilutes blended as it scales).
Marketing spend: ~7% of sales normal; Shotgun >10% of its top line (first 3 years on higher side).
CSD: ~8% of revenue today, expected to grow (Merlot/NOI sales from H1 FY27; Shotgun via CSD H2/Q4 FY27).
order book / pipeline / distribution: RTD (Shotgun) distribution: ~9,000 outlets (2,000 added in FY26); target >15,000 by H2 FY27. Total addressable Fratelli universe ~30,000 outlets.
Shotgun present in 18 states; FY27 launches planned in Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Telangana (H1).
Sette 15th-anniversary limited edition: 5 states now → +7 states FY27 (Delhi, Haryana, UP, WB, TN, Karnataka, Maharashtra).
Fratelli Brut (launched Nov'25): 4 states → +14 states FY27.
segment commentary: Premium (>40% of revenue): declined ~15–16% YoY FY26 on regulatory disruptions (Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Delhi); offset partly by Haryana, UP, Kerala, Sikkim.
Luxury (>INR2,000 MRP): +15% YoY; J'NOON +44%; market share >50% in domestic luxury wine.
RTD (Shotgun): ~INR18 cr / ~100,000 cases year 1; market size INR500–600 cr growing ~25% YoY.
CSD: ~8% of revenue, ~45% market share; wine-in-a-can >90% market share in India.
Premium market share ~30%; HoReCa market share ~40%.
growth / optionality: RTD as structural second growth driver (wine-based fit, leverages existing infra/distribution); 3 new Shotgun variants in Q1 FY27.
Wine-in-a-can entering CSD — new channel optionality.
Hospitality project (INR70–80 cr estimate) — DEFERRED ~1 year; review H2 FY27, possible initiation CY27–28. Optionality, not committed.
Long-term aspiration: ~INR500 cr revenue by 2030 at ~20% CAGR.
FTA upside ambiguous — mgmt sees no near-term material impact (90%+ of wine revenue <INR2,000 MRP; RTD unaffected).
margins & cost: GM 79% (Q4 & FY26); guided 76–80% as RTD (GM ~70%) scales.
EBITDA target ~20% (vs current ~breakeven) — to be reached purely via scale/operating leverage; cost base already built to absorb a doubling of business with no major structural change.
Hospitality explicitly NOT a margin lever; efficiency to come from core wine + RTD scale.
Discounting/schemes flat over 2–3 years; mgmt now trying to reduce.
capex: FY26 capex ~INR10 cr (vineyard infra, plant & machinery, operational infra). Major capex cycle "largely behind us"; existing infra to support next 3 years' growth.
FY27: ~INR9 cr earmarked (routine + strategic) — Gaurav guided INR6–10 cr range.
Hospitality: INR70–80 cr estimate, deferred ~1 year.
capital allocation: Growth largely fundable via internal cash generation other than hospitality.
As a listed entity, "many tools available" to raise capital if a compelling opportunity arises (no current plan to raise equity/leverage).
D&A and finance costs rose in FY26 (new assets + borrowings for capacity & working capital).
risks: State excise / regulatory: primary FY26 headwind — disruptions in Maharashtra, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Delhi; revenue is hostage to state-level license renewals and excise policy changes.
Premiumization dependence: thesis leans heavily on luxury/super-premium and RTD outgrowing premium; any reversal pressures both growth and blended GM.
India-EU FTA: potential competition on >INR2,000 MRP segment (mgmt downplays; <10% of wine revenue there).
Weather/agri: El Nino / rainfall risk to vineyards (mitigated by own vineyards + drip irrigation; full canals post heavy FY25 rain).
Execution: Shotgun doubling, multi-state registrations cyclical (bottleneck on outlet ramp).
management tone: Confident but measured. Emphasized "inflection point," cost base ready for 2x volume, and disciplined discounting. Repeatedly anchored on the INR240 cr / 30% growth / net-net breakeven FY27 milestone. Guarded on cost-line detail ("sensitive") and on hospitality timing. Credible on regulatory recovery (Telangana +30% post-license renewal evidenced).
non-obvious takeaways: "Net-net breakeven" (after D&A + finance cost), not just cash/EBITDA breakeven, is the explicit FY27 bar at ~INR240 cr.
RTD GM (~70%) is dilutive to blended GM as it scales — growth engine slightly trades margin for volume.
Shotgun launch-year marketing >10% of its own top line; this elevated spend persists ~3 years, a drag on near-term margin even as revenue scales.
Hospitality (INR70–80 cr) was deferred to prioritize RTD/wine — capital discipline signal, but removes a future revenue/optionality leg from FY27.
Premium segment (>40% of revenue) actually DECLINED ~15% in FY26 — the flat top line masks a sharp premium contraction offset by luxury (+15%) and RTD (new).
challenges → beneficiaries: ✅ Telangana retail license renewal → Fratelli (Telangana +~30% in Q4; recovery tailwind).
⭐ RTD category at ~25% growth (INR500–600 cr market, >1M cases) → Fratelli as wine-based RTD entrant (Shotgun) and >90% wine-in-a-can share.
(FTA, El Nino: monitored, no clear beneficiary call from mgmt.)
qoq log: Q4 FY26 (this call): Rev INR36 cr (+13% YoY); GM 79%; EBITDA −INR3.7 cr (loss halved YoY). FY26: Rev INR184 cr (+1%), EBITDA +INR1 cr (first FY operating breakeven). RTD year 1: ~INR18 cr / ~100k cases. FY27 guidance: +30% rev (~INR240 cr), net-net PAT breakeven, RTD to double. Capex cycle done (~INR9 cr FY27); hospitality (INR70–80 cr) deferred ~1 yr. Luxury +15% (J'NOON +44%); premium −15% on regulatory hits. GM guided 76–80%.

scorecard.piotroski_basis: needs 2 FYs of BS_* -> 0 (real from FY27)
scorecard.pe_basis: TTM trailing (spec band written for forward P/E)
scorecard.notes: growth: insufficient history; share cagr: n/a; promoter: no SHP row

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
